reviewNote: Drafted by Claude for faculty review from the Carson-Newman scenario. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Healthy hypertensive man for a laparoscopic TEP hernia who had residual blockade in PACU in 2019 (TOF 3/4 with fade, SpO2 89%). The surgeon wants a deep block. The CN Emergence rubric case: the scored run starts at the end of surgery with a TOF ratio below 0.9.

decision.rationale: Elective, optimized; plan quantitative monitoring and sugammadex.

redFlags.finding: Prior residual neuromuscular blockade in PACU
redFlags.evidence: 2019 PACU note: weak, SpO2 89%, TOF 3/4 with fade after neostigmine; patient remembers it.
redFlags.implication: Repeat risk, especially with the deep block the surgeon wants.
redFlags.action: Quantitative TOF monitoring throughout, reverse with sugammadex dosed to depth, confirm TOF ratio 0.9 or more before extubation.

redFlags.finding: Surgeon requests a deep block for TEP
redFlags.implication: Deep block at closure; neostigmine will not reverse it.
redFlags.action: Rocuronium titrated to PTC, sugammadex 4 mg/kg for deep block, monitor until the end.

planItems.item: Quantitative TOF monitoring from induction to extubation
Volatile off, reverse with sugammadex to depth, TOF ratio 0.9 or more, adequate spontaneous ventilation before extubation
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision

boothComplications.why: Emergence at a light plane after extubation
Opioid plus residual weakness after extubation

cnRubric.title: Carson-Newman rubric: Emergence, residual blockade
cnRubric.note: The scored run starts at the END of the case: intubated, on sevoflurane, TOF ratio below 0.9.
